---
name: apple-hig
description: Use when designing, implementing, or reviewing interfaces for iOS, iPadOS, macOS, tvOS, visionOS, watchOS, CarPlay, or other Apple system experiences using Apple's Human Interface Guidelines. Routes to current platform, foundation, pattern, component, input, and technology guidance.
license: MIT
metadata:
  author: AyushRajSinghParihar
  source: https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines
---

# Apple Human Interface Guidelines

Use the relevant Apple guidance to make concrete design decisions. This package
contains a router, 13 family routes, 158 operational topic skills, and supporting
article-level references. It is
independent of Apple. The sources are a dated English HIG snapshot; check the
official source when a task depends on a newer release or a disputed detail.

## Route the task

1. Identify the target platform, device context, and user task from the request or
   project. Ask for the platform only when it materially affects the answer and
   cannot be inferred. Preserve the user's framework and product requirements.
2. Select the relevant family below and read that family's `SKILL.md`. Follow its
   link to the exact topic procedure under `.topics/` and read that `SKILL.md`.
   Apply its decision procedure, then consult its supporting article for facts
   and platform qualifications. Topic skills are explicitly read by installed
   file path; automatic nested discovery is not required.
   For platform support or product-feasibility decisions, first read each relevant
   platform's Getting started procedure, then the specific component or technology
   procedure. Check both the platform model and the surface's support limits.
3. For an exact component, technology, or unfamiliar term, search the
   [complete topic index](references/topic-index.md). It links directly to local
   topic procedures. Enter the procedure before its supporting reference. Do not
   load the full corpus for a narrow question.
   For a screenshot-specific or animated example, also consult its
   [original visual explanation](references/media/index.md) when available.
4. Apply shared guidance and the target platform's documented differences. A
   missing platform subsection means no additional rule is stated; it does not
   prove support, nonapplicability, or identical behavior across platforms.
5. Compose families when the task crosses them: a component can also require
   accessibility, typography, localization, input, or system-experience guidance.
   Map the brief's material decisions to their owning topics. Read the owning
   procedure for each explicit concern, such as privacy or accessibility, as well
   as the affected components; a neighboring procedure's reminder is insufficient.
   Use [platform and task routes](references/platforms-and-tasks.md) when useful.
   In a review, map each supplied control to its candidate component procedure
   even when markup or behavior is missing. Use it to frame inspection questions;
   missing evidence neither proves a defect nor removes that control from scope.

All paths are relative to **this installed package**, not the shell's current
directory. No Python, network, sibling skill installation, or authoring cache is
required to read the guidance.

| Task | Read this topic skill |
|---|---|
| Platform conventions, design principles, games, device adaptation | [Getting started](subskills/apple-hig-getting-started/SKILL.md) |
| Accessibility, typography, color, materials, layout, localization, privacy | [Foundations](subskills/apple-hig-foundations/SKILL.md) |
| Onboarding, loading, search, sharing, accounts, feedback, media, settings | [Patterns](subskills/apple-hig-patterns/SKILL.md) |
| Charts, images, text views, embedded web content | [Content](subskills/apple-hig-content/SKILL.md) |
| Lists, collections, split views, tab views, disclosure and grouping | [Layout and organization](subskills/apple-hig-layout-and-organization/SKILL.md) |
| Buttons, menus, toolbars, menu bar, ornaments and actions | [Menus and actions](subskills/apple-hig-menus-and-actions/SKILL.md) |
| Sidebars, tab bars, search fields, tokens and path controls | [Navigation and search](subskills/apple-hig-navigation-and-search/SKILL.md) |
| Alerts, sheets, popovers, panels, scrolling and windows | [Presentation](subskills/apple-hig-presentation/SKILL.md) |
| Text fields, pickers, sliders, toggles, selection controls | [Selection and input](subskills/apple-hig-selection-and-input/SKILL.md) |
| Progress, activity, gauges and ratings | [Status](subskills/apple-hig-status/SKILL.md) |
| Widgets, Live Activities, notifications, Siri snippets and system surfaces | [System experiences](subskills/apple-hig-system-experiences/SKILL.md) |
| Touch, keyboard, pointer, focus, eyes, gestures, controllers and sensors | [Inputs](subskills/apple-hig-inputs/SKILL.md) |
| Apple Pay, purchases, Siri, VoiceOver, AI, CarPlay and integrations | [Technologies](subskills/apple-hig-technologies/SKILL.md) |

## Perform the requested work

Inspect the supplied brief, flow, code, specification or image before deciding
what is wrong or choosing a framework. Use the user's requested mode:

- **Design:** produce an implementable specification or interaction/state model
  from the topic's decision procedure, with concrete transitions and acceptance
  checks. Connect choices to the user's task and target platform.
- **Implement:** prefer the project's native system components when they supply
  the needed behavior. HIG explains experience requirements; verify API names,
  availability, and code against the appropriate SDK documentation. Make the
  authorized changes in the existing stack; a prose explanation alone does not
  complete an implementation request.
- **Review:** describe the observed problem, its effect, the relevant HIG rule,
  and a concrete correction. Separate source-backed findings from your own
  suggested improvements. Do not invent violations without inspecting evidence.
- **Adapt:** preserve the product task, data and useful state while applying the
  destination platform's interaction model. Patch the supplied artifact or give
  an explicit before/after contract when a design specification is requested.

Topic procedures are framework agnostic. Their worked examples and pseudocode
teach decisions, not a requirement to replace the project's technology. Load
related procedures only for a decision that actually depends on them.

Complete the topic's observable checks and report passed, failed and not executed
separately. Reading a file, citing Apple, or proposing a test does not establish
runtime behavior. Static code or screenshots cannot prove assistive-technology
order, native rendering, physical comfort, haptics, or SDK compilation.

Include official article/section links for material recommendations. Preserve
qualifications such as “consider,” “prefer,” and “avoid”; do not turn design
advice into invented universal requirements. Retain units and platform scope for
numerical specifications. If source passages conflict, describe the conflict
and the conservative application rather than silently changing the source.

## Source boundaries

This is comprehensive local guidance, not a verbatim Apple manual or an SDK API
reference. Original media explanations are supplementary to article references;
the source page remains useful for visual demonstrations. Source snapshots and
review status live in the repository's coverage report, outside ordinary skill
loading. Do not infer that a source has been independently reviewed just because
its local file exists.

Historical `navigation-bars` links now resolve to current Toolbars guidance;
`in-app-purchase` resolves to Apple In-App Purchase. The old Touch Bar and Messages
for Business HIG pages were unavailable at this snapshot. Do not fabricate their
current rules. Translations, archived pages, and complete linked SDK/WWDC libraries
are outside the source boundary.

Platform: iOS. Current shortcut asks users to supply a database row ID, repeats the app name three times and fails silently if the requested list is missing. People commonly add milk to their shared weekly list while hands are occupied.

description: Use when designing widgets, Live Activities, controls, notifications, App Shortcuts, Siri snippets, watch complications/faces, status bars, or tvOS Top Shelf.

# Apple HIG: Select the system surface before designing its content

Use this family to select and compose topic procedures. Infer the platform and
requested work from the supplied project; preserve its framework and constraints.

## Work through the decision

1. Decide whether the task needs a widget, ongoing Live Activity, notification, Siri snippet or another system-owned surface. Enter that surface’s procedure before fitting an app screen into it.
2. Specify the useful glance/action, data freshness and deep-link destination. Respect the surface’s update, interaction, presentation and privacy constraints rather than assuming full-app behavior.
3. Cover the relevant family/size, appearance, redaction, account and unavailable-data contexts. Shared surfaces require explicit decisions about whose information may be visible.
4. Deliver a surface/content/state contract and preview/check matrix; preserve documented platform support and unresolved source conflicts.

## Enter the topic procedure

Read the selected topic’s SKILL.md before its supporting guidance. For a review,
inspect actual evidence and return findings; for an implementation request, make
the authorized change; for design or adaptation, produce a usable specification
or patch. Load related topics only when the chosen procedure calls for them.

- [App Shortcuts](.topics/apple-hig-app-shortcuts/SKILL.md)
- [Complications](.topics/apple-hig-complications/SKILL.md)
- [Controls](.topics/apple-hig-controls/SKILL.md)
- [Live Activities](.topics/apple-hig-live-activities/SKILL.md)

- [Status bars](.topics/apple-hig-status-bars/SKILL.md)

- [Watch faces](.topics/apple-hig-watch-faces/SKILL.md)
- [Widgets](.topics/apple-hig-widgets/SKILL.md)

## Completion evidence

Report the concrete decisions or changes, their source support, and which checks
passed, failed or were not executed. A source citation or a list of links is not
the requested work product. Retain platform exceptions and unresolved source
conflicts; the absence of a platform subsection does not establish support.

name: apple-hig-app-shortcuts
description: Use when creating, reviewing, or adapting discoverable App Shortcuts, activation phrases, optional parameters, and spoken or visual responses.
---

# Expose a complete task beyond the app

Read [the App Shortcuts guide](../../references/app-shortcuts.md). The workflow is application advice; distinguish App Shortcuts from App Intents actions available for custom Mac shortcuts.

Inspect common tasks, intent/entity model, required inputs, invocation surfaces, platform, and create/review/adapt request. Determine which task can finish in context and which must open relevant app content. Record existing intent behavior; do not assume a phrase demonstrates successful execution.

Choose important tasks within the supplied-shortcut limit, evaluating common app schemas where relevant. Keep phrases natural, memorable, and app-named without implying many parameters. An App Shortcut can expose one optional parameter with predictable options; clarify omitted values with a likely default/short alternatives and gather further required details later. Supply complete spoken dialogue for eyes-away devices. Use a snippet for static outcome/confirmation and a Live Activity for evolving bounded progress. Teach availability contextually rather than through repeated unsolicited promotion.

Implement the authorized intent/phrase/response behavior or specify invocation-to-outcome contracts; reviews identify concrete ambiguity, missing input, or incomplete audio output. Do not promise App Shortcuts on Mac/tvOS: Mac App Intents can remain usable in user-composed shortcuts.

**Worked transformation:** Before: “Reserve a desk with Campus” implies three simultaneous parameters and shows only a visual success checkmark. Decision: invocation complexity and audio-only output conceal essential booking details. After: expose a predictable optional location, gather missing time/details in subsequent steps, and speak the actual booking outcome while showing a concise result.

Deliver the artifact, phrases, parameters/defaults, app-opening boundary, and audio/visual responses. Verify omitted/ambiguous inputs, cancellation, entity removal, and eyes-away comprehension. Fail for claiming success before completion, missing essential spoken information, or unsupported surface promises. Siri/Spotlight discovery and native execution require actual client evidence.

Load [snippets](../apple-hig-snippets/SKILL.md), [live-activities](../apple-hig-live-activities/SKILL.md), or [siri](../../../apple-hig-technologies/.topics/apple-hig-siri/SKILL.md) according to the response task.

# App Shortcuts Source: [Apple Human Interface Guidelines](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/app-shortcuts) Snapshot: 2026-10-25. Original implementation guidance derived from the source. App Shortcuts expose important app actions and content through Siri, Spotlight, Shortcuts, the Action button, and Apple Pencil squeeze. They arrive with installation and can become personalized after use. App Intents define the actions, and each shortcut can combine steps into one task. An app can supply up to 10 App Shortcuts; people can also compose their own cross-app shortcuts from its intents. ## Best practices Use app schemas for common domains when they can make content/actions discoverable to Apple Intelligence; App Shortcuts remain useful for distinctive features or content outside schemas. Favor common important tasks that finish in the current context, opening the app for more involved work when helpful. An App Shortcut can expose one optional parameter with predictable familiar options. If omitted, clarify with a likely default and a short alternative set. Keep spoken phrases simple rather than implying several parameters; ask for further required details in later steps. Teach availability with occasional contextual tips during relevant actions. ### Responding to App Shortcuts Use snippets for static results or confirmation options, and Live Activities for evolving progress such as a countdown. Spoken full dialogue must include all essential information for audio-only devices, including AirPods and HomePod. ## Editorial guidelines Create brief memorable activation phrases with natural variants and the app name. Use title case and plural Shortcuts for App Shortcuts and the Shortcuts app. Use lowercase shortcut for an individual generic shortcut. ## Platform considerations No additional visionOS or watchOS rules are specified. App Shortcuts are unsupported in tvOS. ### iOS, iPadOS Shortcuts can appear with an app's Spotlight Top Hit or below in the Shortcuts area. Supply an appropriate SF Symbol or linked-content preview. Put broadly useful tasks first initially; the system later prioritizes frequent use. ### macOS App Shortcuts themselves are unsupported. App Intents actions remain available for people building custom shortcuts in the Mac Shortcuts app. ## Resources Official implementation links and revision metadata follow. #### Related [Siri](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/siri) [Siri Style Guide](https://developer.apple.com/siri/style-guide/) [Shortcuts User Guide](https://support.apple.com/guide/shortcuts/welcome/ios) #### Developer documentation — App Intents — App Intents #### Videos ## Change log Revision dates recorded by Apple: June 8, 2026, January 17, 2025, June 5, 2023.

name: apple-hig-snippets
description: Use when creating, reviewing, or adapting compact App Intents confirmation and result views with spoken responses.
---

# Separate confirmation from a completed result

Read [the snippet guide](../../references/snippets.md). The workflow is application advice; every snippet intent needs a result, with confirmation optional.

Inspect the invoked task, required confirmation, actual outcome, dialogue, custom view, platform, and create/review/adapt request. Establish which information must be understood with no screen. Do not present an accepted request as a completed operation without evidence.

Use confirmation only when a decision is needed, with system Cancel and a concrete action label. Provide the required result with useful outcome and Done. Keep essential spoken dialogue complete for eyes-away use while generally omitting its repeated visible text; the custom view should independently communicate purpose. Fit content within the documented height even with Dynamic Type, and deep-link to longer details instead of cramming them in. Preserve light/dark contrast and margins. Snippets are unsupported on TV/visionOS/watchOS; do not imply audio-only availability proves their visual component support.

Implement the intent confirmation/result or specify dialogue/view/action states; reviews identify missing results, premature success, or incomprehensible audio. Use Live Activities instead for evolving progress rather than a static result that appears current forever.

**Worked transformation:** Before: a reservation shortcut shows `Proceed`, repeats all spoken text visually, and disappears after confirmation without a result. Decision: confirmation is not completion and the compact view lacks independent hierarchy. After: use `Reserve Desk`, speak essential location/time and outcome, show a compact reservation result, and link full details.

Deliver the artifact, confirmation criteria, primary label, complete dialogue, result, and detail link. Verify cancel/confirm, failure, large text height, audio-only comprehension, and long details. Fail for no result, false success, required information omitted from speech, or overflowing custom content. Native intent/snippet/Siri execution remains separate from static checks.

Load [app-shortcuts](../apple-hig-app-shortcuts/SKILL.md) for invocation or [live-activities](../apple-hig-live-activities/SKILL.md) for continuing progress.

Use this family to select and compose topic procedures. Infer the platform and

## Work through the decision

1. Identify the product benefit and capability prerequisites before entering the technology-specific procedure. Avoid adding a system integration solely to decorate an existing flow.
2. Define consent/account/capability availability and the meaningful result, cancel, failure and recovery paths applicable to that integration. Keep sensitive information and system ownership clear.
3. Preserve supplied branding, hardware and platform qualifications. HIG states experience expectations; verify current APIs against implementation documentation when writing framework-specific code.
4. Deliver an integration contract or correction in the existing stack, with source-supported choices, fallbacks and evidence limits. Do not claim a payment, health, spatial or connected-device runtime test from a static specimen.

name: apple-hig-siri
description: Use when designing or reviewing Siri/App Intents actions, app entities and contextual references, relevant donation/indexing, spoken dialogue, snippets, or App Shortcuts.
---

# Expose useful intent and make spoken results stand alone

Read [Siri](../../references/siri.md). Inspect popular tasks, domain objects, hands-free/device context, existing intents/entities, response dialogue, and requested design/review/adaptation. Preserve the existing stack and verify current App Intents/schema availability; do not assume Siri understands private app capabilities without explicit integration.

Choose high-value actions and familiar audience nouns/verbs. Adopt existing domain schemas where they fit; use App Shortcuts for useful functions beyond those domains. Annotate onscreen objects with entities so contextual references resolve, index personally relevant content, and donate actual actions/interests rather than indiscriminately promoting everything. Keep ads, purchase pitches, and marketing out of delivered content.

Prefer built-in responses unless they cannot meet the task. Define required parameters and specific follow-up questions that name the requested object. When options are too numerous, narrow openly instead of reciting a long list. Provide audible and visual forms, with spoken text sufficient by itself. Optional snippets may be omitted, so essential information cannot exist only in a visual property.

Keep responses brief, device-independent unless the device is verified, and free of repeated app attribution supplied by the system. Consider bystanders, parental controls, and precise current-problem recovery. Refer to Siri by name, preserve localized invocation conventions, and avoid reserved system/emergency behavior or impersonating Apple.

**Worked transformation:** Before, a recipe shortcut says “Done—see this” while showing the only result in a card, indexes every promotion, and asks “Which one?” without context. Decision: hands-free results need independent meaning and relevant content. After, the response names the selected recipe/action, the follow-up asks which saved recipe is intended, and donation/indexing focuses on actual saved or used content rather than ads.

Deliver action/entity/parameter and audible/visual response contracts or implementation. Fail if essential results vanish without a snippet, ambiguous references trigger wrong actions, or dialogue requires unseen context. Source/code review cannot establish actual Siri recognition, entity resolution, system suggestions, or natural-language quality; list supported-device tests separately.

Use [Action button](../../../apple-hig-inputs/.topics/apple-hig-action-button/SKILL.md) for hardware shortcut invocation and [Writing](../../../apple-hig-foundations/.topics/apple-hig-writing/SKILL.md) for concise follow-up/recovery language.

# Snippets Source: [Apple Human Interface Guidelines](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/snippets) Snapshot: 2026-10-25. Original implementation guidance derived from the source. A snippet responds to a Siri, Spotlight, or Shortcuts action with a compact result or confirmation. App Intents define its task. Confirmation can offer choices and cancel/confirm; a result provides the outcome without requiring further action. Every snippet intent shows a result, with confirmation optional. ## Anatomy The intent supplies spoken dialogue, included as text above the custom view by default. The custom view conveys information and can include relevant actions. Confirmation adds system Cancel and a customizable primary button; result adds Done. ## Best practices Keep contrast and margins clear in light/dark appearances. Custom content must not exceed 400 pt high, accounting for Dynamic Type. Deep-link to longer result details. Use a concrete primary label such as the actual action rather than OK/Proceed; Continue is the default when none is given. Keep spoken dialogue complete for eyes-away use, but generally omit its visible repetition and make the custom view communicate purpose independently. ## Platform considerations No additional iOS, iPadOS, or macOS rules are specified. Snippets are unsupported in tvOS, visionOS, and watchOS. ## Resources Official implementation links and revision metadata follow. #### Related [Siri](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/siri) [App Shortcuts](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/app-shortcuts) [Live Activities](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/live-activities) #### Developer documentation #### Videos ## Change log Revision dates recorded by Apple: June 8, 2026.

# Siri Source: [Apple Human Interface Guidelines](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/siri) · Retrieved 2026-10-25. This is original application guidance based on the source text. Independent media review is recorded separately in the coverage report. Siri supports information and quick actions through voice and system entry points, including the Siri app and Dynamic Island interactions. On supported devices, Siri AI uses Apple Intelligence for natural-language/contextual actions across apps and onscreen content. ## Getting your app to work with Siri Expose app actions as intents and content as entities through App Intents; the system otherwise lacks specific awareness of the app’s capabilities. Siri, Spotlight, and Shortcuts can then surface appropriate actions/content. Adopt existing domain schemas, such as email/music/photos, to use built-in natural-language and contextual logic. ### Sharing contextual information Annotate views/content with app entities so Siri understands references to onscreen objects. Donate relevant entities to the on-device Spotlight index for search and Siri. Donate actual user actions/interests as intents to inform appropriate future suggestions. ## Best practices Prioritize popular actions and the device/location/hands-free contexts where people need them. Use the audience’s familiar nouns and verbs. Index personally relevant content such as favorites, searches, bookmarks, and wishlists instead of indiscriminately donating everything; whole catalogs can be justified for email/messages. Keep advertisements, marketing, and purchase pitches out of Siri-delivered content. Prefer built-in responses unless they cannot meet the need. ## Customizing your app’s experience with Siri Use App Shortcuts for custom functions beyond existing schema domains. Optional intent/entity properties can improve schema responses with static or interactive snippets, such as playback controls. The system may omit optional visual properties in some contexts, so essential information cannot depend on their appearance. Write clear, brief response dialogue and specific follow-up questions that identify the object being requested. Remove repeated detail and humor that become irritating. Provide both audible and visual forms; spoken output must stand alone. Avoid unnecessary gender assumptions, use open-ended narrowing when options are too numerous to read, and keep wording device-independent unless a specific device is verified. Omit the app name because the system supplies attribution. Respect parental controls, avoid offensive speech, and remember bystanders can hear responses. Replace generic failures with a precise explanation of the current problem. ## Editorial guidelines Call Siri by name rather than gendered pronouns. Do not impersonate Siri or Apple, reproduce reserved system behavior, or claim reserved phrases such as emergency calls. Siri remains untranslated; only the greeting in the invocation localizes. The source’s approved groupings are: |Locales|Invocation| |---|---| |ar_AE, ar_SA|يا Siri| |da_DK, sv_SE|Hej Siri| |de_AT, de_CH, de_DE; en_AU, en_CA, en_GB, en_IE, en_IN, en_NZ, en_SG, en_US, en_ZA; ja_JP, tr_TR|Hey Siri| |es_CL, es_ES, es_MX, es_US|Oye Siri| |fi_FI, nb_NO, no_NO|Hei Siri| |fr_BE, fr_CA, fr_CH, fr_FR|Dis Siri| |it_CH, it_IT|Ehi Siri| |ko_KR|Siri야| |ms_MY|Hai Siri| |nl_BE|Hé, Siri| |nl_NL|Hé Siri| |pt_BR|E aí Siri| |ru_RU|привет Siri| |th_TH|หวัดดี Siri| |zh_CN|嘿Siri| |zh_HK|喂 Siri| |zh_TW|嘿 Siri| ## Resources Consult the [official article](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/siri) for linked Apple design assets and implementation resources. #### Related The official article links the adjacent HIG topics relevant to this guidance. #### Developer documentation Use the framework references linked by Apple for current API availability and implementation details. #### Videos Apple’s linked design sessions provide demonstrations and additional implementation context; no video review is implied here. ## Change log Source revision dates: June 8, 2026, June 5, 2023, May 2, 2023.

item.text: The brief identifies three problems: a database ID exposed to users, repeated app attribution, and silent failure when a list is missing. I’ll replace these with named lists, a simple activation phrase, and spoken outcomes that make sense without looking at a screen.

item.command:
/bin/bash -lc "cat > interface.md <<'EOF'
# Grocery app: Add Item App Shortcut

## Scope and discovery

Target: iOS. Preserve adding groceries to a shared weekly list while hands are occupied. This is an interaction specification, not SDK implementation. The app's name is unspecified; "'`{AppName}` below means its actual localized display name, not literal placeholder text.

Supply one broadly useful App Shortcut, **Add Item**, first in the app'"'s initial shortcut ordering. Make it available with installation, without requiring people to build a custom shortcut first. Use a checklist SF Symbol for the system entry. Siri, Spotlight, and Shortcuts are the intended discovery/invocation surfaces; actual placement and personalization belong to the system and are not guaranteed.

After the second successful in-app add to the same list, show one dismissible contextual tip: “Add groceries with Siri. Try ‘Add an item with {AppName}.’” Offer “View in Shortcuts” to the app's shortcut collection where supported. Record dismissal; do not repeat automatically. The two-add threshold is a product choice, not an Apple requirement. Keep the ordinary in-app add flow available.

Activation phrase variants:

- “Add an item with {AppName}.”
- “Add groceries with {AppName}.”
- “Add to {List} with {AppName}.”

Each phrase includes the app name once. Do not put the app name in app-authored follow-up or result dialogue; system attribution supplies it. Do not imply that item, quantity, and list must all be spoken in the activation phrase.

## Action and entity contract

Expose an Add Item action through App Intents. Assess existing domain schemas during implementation; no matching grocery schema or API availability is established by the supplied files.

The shortcut exposes only one optional parameter: **List**. Options are familiar writable grocery-list entities, shown and spoken by display name, for example “Weekly groceries.” Internal stable IDs resolve identity but are never requested, displayed, or read aloud.
